caption: A swan glides across a still lake at sunset, and its reflection glides beneath it with the orange sky behind both.

sa.check: A swan glides across a lake.
The orange sky is behind both.

pc.expect: The reflected swan is directly under the real one and moves with it, breaking up only in the swan's own ripples.
pc.fail: It is offset; or stays still while the swan glides; or it is broken on flat water ahead.

pc.expect: The reflection is inverted and joined at the waterline, with the orange sky reflected around it.
pc.fail: It is upright; or detached; or the reflected sky is a different colour.

pc.expect: The reflection does not move on its own.
pc.fail: It moves with the swan still; or drifts across the lake.

pc.expect: The water is liquid: ripples spread from the swan and the surface elsewhere stays flat.
pc.fail: The surface is rigid; or ripples run ahead of the swan; or the water leaps.

pc.expect: One swan and one reflection; the reflection stays on the water.
pc.fail: A second swan appears; or the reflection rises off the water; or the swan vanishes; or the reflection becomes solid.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The swan's plumage and the sky stay the same.
pc.fail: The plumage changes; or the sky changes colour abruptly; or the shore rearranges.

note: Self-driven animal: where it goes and how it moves are not judged. Only the reflection's relation to it is.
